_comment: Canonicalization-benchmark layer on top of the 500-entry ml-ai-dataset, built the same way as ../../propositions.json (physics v0.2): a curated subset chosen specifically because it exhibits the same failure patterns (specialization-vs-identity, apparent-contradiction-from-missing-phase/context, genuine scientific-revision contradiction, compatible siblings, hyperedges). Most entries reuse the exact 'claim' text from ../dataset.json (noted via source_id) with an added context field; two are new (BN_ORIG / BN_REVISED) because the raw dataset's single BatchNorm-mechanism entries needed to be split into two atomic, directly-opposable propositions.

propositions.statement: Momentum accumulates an exponentially decaying moving average of past gradients to accelerate convergence and dampen oscillation in narrow loss-surface valleys.
AdaGrad adapts each parameter's learning rate by dividing by the square root of the sum of its past squared gradients, giving infrequently-updated parameters larger effective steps.
AdaGrad's accumulated squared-gradient denominator grows monotonically, causing its effective learning rate to shrink toward zero over long training runs.
RMSProp fixes AdaGrad's vanishing-learning-rate problem by using an exponentially decaying moving average of squared gradients instead of a cumulative sum.
Adam combines a momentum-style first moment estimate with an RMSProp-style adaptive second moment estimate, plus bias correction for both.
Dropout randomly zeroes a fraction of unit activations during training, preventing co-adaptation of neurons and acting as an implicit ensemble of subnetworks.
At test time, dropout is disabled and activations are scaled to match the expected magnitude seen during training.
DropConnect generalizes dropout by randomly zeroing individual weights (connections) rather than whole unit activations.

propositions.notes: Ioffe & Szegedy 2015's original hypothesis, now empirically challenged by BN_REVISED.
propositions.statement: Batch normalization improves training primarily by reducing internal covariate shift: the change in the distribution of each layer's inputs during training caused by updates to preceding layers.

propositions.notes: Santurkar et al. 2018's empirical finding, which directly challenges BN_ORIG as an explanation of the SAME phenomenon (why BatchNorm improves training) -- not a different-context reconciliation like the water/dropout/attention pairs. Deliberately given the SAME (empty) context as BN_ORIG: this is a genuine contradiction between two claimed mechanisms, not an apparent one resolvable by adding a condition.
propositions.statement: Batch normalization's main benefit is smoothing the optimization landscape, not reducing internal covariate shift.
ResNet's residual (skip) connections let a layer learn a residual function relative to its input, mitigating vanishing gradients and enabling training of networks over 100 layers deep.
DenseNet connects each layer to every other layer in a feed-forward fashion within a block, encouraging feature reuse and alleviating vanishing gradients.
Self-attention computes pairwise interactions between all token pairs, costing O(n^2) time and memory in sequence length n.
Sparse attention patterns restrict each token to attend to a limited set of positions, reducing the quadratic cost of full self-attention for long sequences.
BERT uses a bidirectional Transformer encoder pretrained with masked language modeling and next-sentence prediction.
GPT uses a unidirectional (causal) Transformer decoder pretrained by next-token prediction.
Deep Q-Networks approximate the Q-function with a deep neural network, enabling Q-learning to scale to high-dimensional inputs like raw pixels, such as Atari games.

Network pruning removes individual weights or entire structural units, such as neurons, channels, or filters, from a trained network, reducing its size and, for structured pruning, potentially its inference compute.
